title: Microstructural geometry parameterization
action: Determine the characteristic dimensions for the two microstructures from the paper's description: normalized steel – ferrite sphere radius a = 10 µm, compute the pearlite shell volume factor K; hot-rolled steel – ferrite band width = 60 µm, pearlite band width = 20 µm. Write these parameters to a JSON file.
description: Extract and document the microstructural dimensions that serve as inputs to the diffusion models.

title: Compute homogenization distances
action:
Implement the analytical diffusion models for the two microstructures:
- Normalized case: spherical diffusion from a well-stirred reservoir of limited volume. Solve the series expansion to find the dimensionless time τ at which the fractional approach to equilibrium is 0.95, then compute √(Dt) = √(τ) × a.
- Hot-rolled case: finite one-dimensional slab with reflections. Using the band geometry, compute the concentration profile via error‑function superposition and reflections, and determine the √(Dt) at which the distribution is essentially uniform (for example, when the carbon concentration variation across the ferrite band becomes negligible).
Report both √(Dt) values in micrometers within a single JSON file.
description: Produces a JSON file containing the two computed homogenization distances.
